stories.primary_headline: Anti-CEC stir | Delhi Police registers cases, arrests 5 persons over attacks on protesters

primary_source.headline: Anti-CEC stir | Delhi Police registers cases, arrests 5 persons over attacks on protesters
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Delhi Police has registered at least 10 FIRs and arrested five people in connection with alleged harassment and assaults on protesters demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with several social media posts accusing right-wing activists of targeting demonstrators, officials said on Sunday.The cases were registered between October 11 and 14 at Connaught Place and Kamla Market police stations after videos and posts highlighting alleged attacks on protesters circulated on social media.At least five people have been arrested in two separate cases, a senior police officer said.According to the police, an FIR was registered at Connaught Place police station on October 13 in connection with an incident flagged through social media handles.Delhi Police registers four FIRs against 'rumour-mongers', Pak social media handles under scannerGaurav was arrested in the case, while efforts are underway to trace his alleged accomplices.A group of men was seen assaulting a protester while daring others to call them "cockroaches". One of the men was also heard threatening to beat up anyone who spoke against the prime minister or the police.In another case, registered at Kamla Market police station on October 11, four people were arrested after a video purportedly showing individuals harassing and assaulting protesters went viral.Police took suo motu cognisance of the incident and initiated legal action against those allegedly involved.The list of cases also includes multiple FIRs registered at Connaught Place police station on October 13 and 14 over incidents highlighted in social media posts and videos. Police are examining CCTV footage to identify those involved, establish the sequence of events and determine the roles of the suspected accused.EC-SIR row: Delhi Police take down 300 social media for spreading 'rumours'Several social media posts have alleged that right-wing activists assaulted or harassed protesters during the demonstrations.The footage and allegations are being examined by police as they work to identify the people involved and establish the circumstances surrounding the incidents.The police action comes amid a wider scrutiny of online content related to the protests, with authorities also investigating posts allegedly circulating misinformation, rumours and fabricated videos.Some social media accounts have shared claims of police brutality against demonstrators, which investigators are examining to establish their authenticity.In one of the cases, police have sought information from social media platform X to identify a user accused of uploading videos that they suspect were fabricated and circulated to disrupt public order.Police have identified more than 37 social media accounts, including over 17 allegedly linked to right-wing groups, for purportedly circulating misleading content related to the protests, a source in the police said.Takedown notices have been issued to more than 17 handles, including those linked to right-wing groups, and action has been initiated under relevant provisions of the Information Technology Act and other laws for allegedly inciting people and disrupting law and order, they said.Some right-wing accounts allegedly shared posts and reels targeting protesters and presenting the demonstrations in a misleading manner, while other users circulated videos purportedly showing police brutality against demonstrators.Investigators are examining the content to verify its authenticity and identify those responsible, the officials added.The protests in the national capital have been organised over demands for Kumar's resignation and a rollback of the SIR exercise. Further investigation in the cases is underway.

Explained | Govt caps trade margins on 137 cancer drugs at 30%: NPPA
Government caps trade margins on 137 anti-cancer drugs at 30%

brief_bullets: The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers has announced a price cap of 30 per cent on the trade margins of 137 cancer medicines, over the cost of the drug at the first point, either to a stockist/distributor or the hospital.

These margins will apply when the drugs are sold directly to them by a manufacturer. The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), in an order dated October 17, has directed manufacturers to submit the revised MRP within seven days. "The revised prices shall come into effect from November 9," the gazette notification stated. Impact on cancer drug pricesAn analysis of pharmaceutical market data indicates that non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs carry an average trade mark-up of approximately 170 per cent, with mark-ups of up to 700 per cent in certain cases, according to an NPPA meeting conducted earlier.
why_it_matters_bullets: Marks an important milestone in treatment development, shaping clinical guidelines and patient standard-of-care.

stories.primary_headline: Mysuru Dasara 2026 | Kambala turns Saathgalli into mini Tulu Naadu

primary_source.headline: Mysuru Dasara 2026 | Kambala turns Saathgalli into mini Tulu Naadu
primary_source.content: Mysuru: Amid all the opposition by activists, two-day Kambala-male buffalo or bulls race which began on Sunday morning, is unravelling mini Tulu Naadu at Saathgalli in Mysuru. A sea of people of all age groups are rushing to the mini fair. They are thrilled to witness 150 pairs of bulls who are splashing the water to the height of upto 7 feet and crossing 145 meter length and 30 meter width Kambala track in lightning speed within seconds. While the races in six segments began around 10 am, Chief Minister D K Shivakumar formally inaugurated it at around 7.30 pm and witnessed the race for about an hour. CM D K Shivakumar said "Kambala is a harvest festival of Coastal region. They started it 800 years praying Kadri Manjunathswamy to protect farmers. In order to showcase all cultures during Naada Habba Mysuru Dasara we are hosting Kambala here to foster the culture. They have put sensors to record the time taken by each buffalo and one had crossed track in nine seconds."Forums urge Kambala buffalo owners to stay away from Mysuru event amid droughtPuttur MLA Ashok Kumar Rai said, "We hosted Kambala in Bengaluru last year. We had planned to host it during Dasara in Mysuru last year itself. We are happy to introduce this coastal culture of Kambala to the people of Mysuru region during Dasara this year." He urged CM for the opportunity to host it in all possible districts across the State.Ashok Kumar Rai said, "The race will conclude on Monday evening. A reward of 16 gram gold, 8 gram gold and 4 gram gold will be given for those winning first, second and third prizes respectively. The owners of each pair of Buffaloes need atleast Rs 3 lakh to bring them here. They spend atleast Rs 12 lakh a year to nourish them. The owners of these buffaloes don't participate in Kambala for prize but to keep up their family name and carry forward the legacy of this culture."He informed, "The bulls which arrived on Saturday evening will be leaving on Tuesday morning. About 5000 assistants have accompanied them. They are accommodated with the buffaloes at the venue. They have brought the food and water for the buffaloes. The state government is spending about Rs 3 crore and they have made all arrangements. They are giving an honorarium of Rs 65,000 for each pair of bigger bulls and Rs 50,000 per pair for smaller bulls."Environmentalists, farmers hold mega protest opposing Kambala amid droughtEven as about half a million liter water is required per day, they have drilled two borewells. He claimed that since it has rained well, the tracks are naturally full and the water consumption has reduced. Ashok Rai also said that the arrangement has been done to accommodate about 15,000 people, but atleast 20,000 people are witnessing the event at a time. By 12 noon 75,000 people had witnessed it at the venue; and 2 million people had watched it online by 2 pm on Sunday.Besides races, people are even enjoying coastal style food including varieties of fishes, Kori rotti, Neerdose at food mela hosted by people of coastal region including those from Mangaluru. Besides grabbing video of races, people are also clicking photos and selfies with buffaloes.85-year-old Lakshmi from Shirsi who had come for Dasara to her daughter's house in Mysuru said, "I had never seen it live though I had seen it on TV and internet, so I was keen to witness it."Mysuru district police led by SP Mallikarjun Balanandi said that they have deployed about 1500 cops for the security to the overnight event. They have installed 50 CCTV cameras and are using four drones too.

primary_source.headline: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina
primary_source.content: Facing a slump in the polls, Argentina’s president is making economic attacks on the islands’ oil industry, and suggesting its key fisheries industry could be next A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly. Outside, it was a typically blowy early evening. It may nominally be spring in the south Atlantic, but Stanley harbour, with its dark grey water speckled with historical shipwrecks, was a cauldron of swells and churn.Six of the assembly’s eight members – five men, one woman – waited patiently at a row of desks and microphones. The heating had been turned up to just short of uncomfortable. Behind them, a portrait of King Charles. From the other walls, dusty photographs of governors peered down on the scene. stories.primary_headline: Private complaints over false election affidavits need no official sanction: Supreme Court

primary_source.headline: Private complaints over false election affidavits need no official sanction: Supreme Court
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Private citizens can file criminal complaints against candidates for submitting false affidavits with their nomination papers, the Supreme Court has ruled, clarifying that no prior sanction or complaint from the Election Commission or any public servant is required.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu held that an offence under Section 125-A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, does not fall within the restrictive ambit of Section 195 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. EC-SIR row | ‘Undermining EC, Supreme Court is not a right’: Harvard scholars warns against erosion of public trust in IndiaThe non-obstante clause in Section 125-A and the deliberate legislative omission to include it in Section 195 CrPC mean courts can take cognizance of such complaints lodged by private persons under Section 200 CrPC, the court said.The ruling came in an appeal filed by Rajkumar Madki challenging a March 7, 2025, judgment of the Karnataka High Court. The High Court had quashed Madki’s August 2023 private complaint against Dr Shailendra Beldale, the MLA from Bidar, alleging that the legislator had given a false residential address in the affidavit accompanying his 2023 nomination papers.The October 16, 2026 decision settles a substantial question of law of general public importance that had not been previously decided by the court.The High Court had held that only the Election Commission could complain of an offence under Section 125-A and that a voter’s remedy was limited to an election petition. The Supreme Court disagreed on the legal point, observing that courts cannot expand the list of offences requiring a public servant’s complaint by implication.“The prohibition on a court taking cognizance… is restricted to the offences specifically enumerated therein,” the bench said. Supreme Court seeks replies from CEC Gyanesh Kumar, others on plea filed by Rahul Gandhi, oppn leadersIt noted that Section 125-A is of relatively recent origin and that Parliament could have amended Section 195 CrPC if it intended to restrict such prosecutions. Guidelines or press notes issued by the Election Commission, the court added, cannot bind judicial interpretation of the statute.Despite upholding the maintainability of private complaints in principle, the apex court declined to revive the specific case against Beldale, represented by senior advocate Anand Sanjay M Nuli. It found that the documents on record effectively rebutted the allegation of false declaration of residence and that the prospect of conviction was remote. Continuing the trial, the court said, would only waste judicial time.The High Court’s order quashing the proceedings was therefore left undisturbed, but on different grounds. The Supreme Court made it clear that magistrates retain full powers to deal with frivolous or harassing complaints if any are filed in future.

stories.primary_headline: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings

primary_source.headline: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
primary_source.content: Anthropic argues that its own workplace trends could be indicators of “how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy,” especially since the company “has thoroughly molded its workflows around AI.” But even if other organizations never embrace AI as thoroughly or in the exact same way as Anthropic, the report offers an intriguing glimpse at how the company currently operates. Notably, Anthropic is making fewer junior hires, with the proportion of junior-level employees in technical departments falling from 21% to 14% since early 2025, and the proportion of junior technical hires falling even more sharply, from 27% to 9%. Anthropic also says that technical teams now represent a smaller share of the overall workforce, falling from 61% to 56% — a trend that it attributes to  “natural expansion of business functions as the company scales,” as well as “coding tools increasingly allowing non-technical employees to make software themselves.” One employee reportedly described an “eternal pressure at Anthropic to move as fast as possible and use Claude for everything.” In an April 2026 survey, 27% of employees said they had become more productive because of Claude  and 20% said their job had shifted “from actually doing work to managing Claudes”; apparently one engineered compared this to babysitting: “When you are babysitting, every child brings to you concerns with an equal demand for your attention and the various [Claudes] also do that.” In fact, the report suggests “human attention and judgement” are becoming a “bottleneck” for productivity, as Claude produces a “deluge” of text that needs to be read and organized. Unsurprisingly, the report argues that AI adoption has made the company more productive, as indicated by “more code per person, closing more sales per rep, and processing more contracts.” The company acknowledges that “more code does not necessarily mean better code or business impact,” but it also hasn’t found any indications that code quality is declining.
